channel.title: Sunwoo Park — Notes on building
channel.description: Long-form essays behind the X threads: craft, systems, and showing up daily.

item.title: Write 50 Posts Before Your First Follower — Sunwoo Park
item.description: Stop waiting for followers to start. Your first 50 posts aren’t for an audience — they’re for you. Voice, detachment from the scoreboard, a body of proof, and editing instincts are all earned through reps.

item.title: The 7-Round Rule: When to Stop Arguing With Yourself — Sunwoo Park
item.description: Red-teaming has a failure mode nobody warns you about: no natural stopping point. Seven rounds max, each attacking a different failure mode. Then freeze the design, write down the reversal condition, and go touch real data.

item.title: Daily Compounding Turned Me From An AI Consumer Into A Builder — Sunwoo Park
item.description: For my first year or two with AI tools, I was a world-class consumer. The shift came from a smaller decision: twenty minutes a day, touching the thing. Compounding only works if you deposit — every day, small amounts, boring amounts.

item.title: Content Needs Release Gates, Not Inspiration — Sunwoo Park
item.description: Content needs release gates, not inspiration. Four gates between an idea and the public: stockpile 12 finished posts, calibrate like a stranger, automate Day 1, and let the 14-day verdict — keep, change, or kill — decide.

item.title: Don't Convince the Customer. Make Betrayal Impossible. — Sunwoo Park
item.description: Don't convince the customer — become the one they can't betray. Three mechanics of unbetrayable trust: costly truth, one small daily promise, co-owned rituals.

item.title: Your AI Doesn't Need More Context. It Needs a Librarian. — Sunwoo Park
item.description: Your AI doesn't need more context. It needs a librarian. Summary notes, daily logs, per-person cards — feed it less, curate what you keep.

item.title: One Finished Video Is a Demo. A Daily Pipeline Is the Product. — Sunwoo Park
item.description: One finished video is a demo. A daily pipeline is the product: a 9:20 AM draft machine, a v1-never-ships rule, and separating deciding from doing — how a solo creator beats the continuity trap.

item.title: Specs Harden in Review, Not in Planning — Sunwoo Park
item.description: My game prototype passed all 44 tests — but the spec hardened in review, not in planning. Three of Codex's 8 review findings became regression tests. A review comment is advice; a test is enforcement. Specs harden when the weak spot gets a guard.

item.title: Your Defaults Are Decisions. Name Them. — Sunwoo Park
item.description: On September 29 I finalized my daily routine v1, and every unmade choice got the same label: “내 기본값.” My default. Naming a default isn't a new decision — it's admitting the one you already made.

item.title: Publish the Process, Not Just the Product. — Sunwoo Park
item.description: Marketing is the hardest part — so I publish the process, not just the product. The wins, the rejections, the pending Vercel token. When you have no track record, “watch me try” is a strategy you can start today.

item.title: Break First, Then Build — Sunwoo Park
item.description: Last night my AI ran five rounds attacking its own plan: the waterfall sequencing broke, the definition broke, the tech assumption broke. What changed wasn’t a patched plan — it was a rebuilt one: a voice demo first. Break first, then build: patch facts, rebuild premises, and let trust compound.
